diagnostic_evidence.quote: so the third term equals zero eventually, and the result is proved

issues.failure_explanation: The tail region is defined through $\vartheta-\vartheta_0=\sqrt N(\theta-\theta_0)$, so $\{\|\vartheta-\vartheta_0\|>1\}=\{\|\theta-\theta_0\|>N^{-1/2}\}$. The proof then bounds it using the event $\{\|\theta-\theta_0\|>1\}$, which is a much smaller set. The localised posterior is only confined to $\|\theta-\theta_0\|\lesssim L\tilde\delta_N\gg N^{-1/2}$, so the third term does not vanish for the reason given. On the complement region the integrand is of size $\sqrt N\|\theta-\theta_0\|$, so the first term is bounded by a factor $\sqrt N$ times the TV distance, not by the TV distance itself.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the estimate with $\sqrt N$ weights on the correct region. Use $\int\|\vartheta-\vartheta_0\|\,d|\tau_N-\bar\tau_N|\le \sqrt N\,\sup_{\bar\Theta_N}\|\theta-\theta_0\|\cdot TV$ plus a Cauchy–Schwarz tail term on $\bar\Theta_N^c$. Both are exponentially small by (tvbd) and Theorem postcont.
issues.overall_effect: The reduction from the full posterior to the localised posterior is not established as written. Every later step that passes through it is therefore unsupported as written (Theorem mainbvm, hence bvminv and ganzwien). The stated rate $e^{-cN\delta_N^2}$ should survive after repair.
issues.title: Wasserstein comparison of full and localised posterior: integration region and TV factor mismatched
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short local recomputation using bounds already in the paper. The conclusion and rate are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: noting that the $C^1([0,T], C^1)$-norm of $V=f'(\tilde u)$ is bounded by a fixed constant $M=M(B)>0$ whenever $\bar \gamma>3+d/2$

issues.failure_explanation: The scalar mean value theorem gives an intermediate point $s=s(t,x)$ that depends on $(t,x)$ and is not controlled. The function $\tilde u=(1-s)u_\theta+s u_{\theta_0}$ then need not be differentiable in $t$ or $x$, and $V=f'(\tilde u)$ need not be in $C^1([0,T],C^1)$. The chain-rule bounds for $V'$ and $\nabla V$ therefore have no justification. Lemma paristexas requires exactly this norm bound. The same pointwise $\tilde u$ is used for the $H^\zeta$ energy estimate behind (h2estimate), where $\|f'(\tilde u)\|_{H^\zeta}$ is bounded.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the pointwise mean value by the integral form $V=\int_0^1 f'(s u_\theta+(1-s)u_{\theta_0})\,ds$. This is smooth and satisfies the same chain-rule bounds. Lemma paristexas and the $H^\zeta$ estimate then apply verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: The stability estimate (dochparis), which verifies Condition E, and the $L^\infty$ Lipschitz bound for Condition D rest on an unjustified regularity claim. The verification of Condition gemol in Theorem bvminv, and so Theorem ganzwien, is affected.
issues.title: Pointwise mean-value potential $f'(\tilde u)$ assumed to have $C^1([0,T],C^1)$ regularity
issues.why_classification: A standard local substitution fixes it, with the same estimates and no change of method or conclusions.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which by (\ref{fishinvbd}) and the Sobolev imbedding theorem defines an element of

issues.failure_explanation: Condition F gives boundedness of $\mathcal I^{-1}$ only on $H^\eta_0$ with $\eta\ge\eta_0$. The bounds $\|\bar e_j\|_{L^2}\lesssim 1$ and $\|\mathbb I(\lambda_j^{-(\kappa+2)/2}\bar e_j)\|\le c$ are justified by an $\mathcal I^{-2}$, $H^{\eta_0}$–$H^{-\eta_0}$ pairing that is not meaningful under the hypotheses. What is available is $\|\bar e_j\|_{L^2}^2\lesssim\lambda_j^{\eta_0+2}$ from (fishinvbd), so the sum in (momhat) converges only if $k>\eta_0+d/2$. The theorem assumes only $k>\eta_0$. Likewise, applying (fishinvbd) to $\psi\in H^{\kappa+2}$ needs $\kappa\ge\eta_0$, which (ks) does not guarantee.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis $\kappa\ge\eta_0$ (e.g. $k>\max(\zeta+5d/2,\eta_0+d/2)$). Redo (momhat) and (fullbd) via (fishinvbd) with the appropriate powers of $\lambda_j$.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, the general Theorem mainbvm is not covered for $\eta_0<k\le\eta_0+d/2$. The uniform moment bounds used in laplaceapp and prop:added-1 are also affected. The reaction–diffusion application is unaffected, because $\eta_0$ can be taken just above $2+d/2$ and then $\kappa\ge\eta_0$.
issues.title: Fisher-information inverse used on $L^2$ and low Sobolev scales although Condition F only gives invertibility for $\eta\ge\eta_0$
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard parameter condition suffices, and the application is unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which converges to zero in $P_{\theta_0}^\mathbb N$-probability as $N \to \infty$ by Theorem \ref{bvminv}.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof after Theorem bvminv treats only $\mathscr W_1(Law(Y_N),Law(Y))\to0$. Theorem bvminv itself states only the Wasserstein limit. The convergence in law of $\sqrt N(u_{\tilde\theta_N}-u_{\theta_0})$ in $\mathscr C$ needs two extra ingredients. One is the linearisation remainder $\sqrt N\|u_{\tilde\theta_N}-u_{\theta_0}-Du_{\theta_0}[\tilde\theta_N-\theta_0]\|_{\mathscr C}=o_P(1)$. The other is the continuous mapping theorem applied to $Du_{\theta_0}:H^{-k-2}\to\mathscr C$ together with the CLT for $\sqrt N(\tilde\theta_N-\theta_0)$ from mainbvm. Neither is given.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a short argument for the remainder. It follows from (meanreg) and the same interpolation and quadratic-remainder estimate used for term I. Then apply the continuous mapping theorem to $Du_{\theta_0}$ and the second limit of Theorem mainbvm.
issues.overall_effect: One of the two advertised conclusions of the main theorem, and the stated consequence that $\sqrt N(u_{\tilde\theta}-u_{\theta_0})$ is uniformly tight and asymptotically Gaussian in the sup-norm, is unsupported as written.
issues.title: Second limit in Theorem ganzwien (posterior mean fluctuations in $\mathscr C$) is never proved
issues.why_classification: The missing argument is a routine adaptation of estimates already in the proof. It is a contained, short addition.
